title: indigo_agent_scripting: indigo_target_altitude() passes the caller's RA/Dec to indigo_radec_to_altaz() without stating or converting the frame
description:
Found 2026-11-19 in ticket ceebf3be. indigo_target_altitude(ra, dec, latitude, longitude) in indigo_drivers/agent_scripting/indigo_agent_scripting.c passes the caller's coordinates straight to indigo_radec_to_altaz(), which expects coordinates of date. Sequencer.js steps wait_until_target_altitude_above() and break_if_target_altitude_below() pass user values, and scheduler tasks pass scheduler_task.ra/dec from @target, which is J2000. If the caller's coordinates are J2000, the altitude is wrong by the precession since J2000 (about 0.36 deg in position, up to roughly 0.3 deg in altitude).
Work: determine what each caller actually passes (Sequencer.js steps, scheduler task wrapper, documented JS API in indigo_docs / agent_scripting README is read-only); decide and document the frame (J2000 is what @target and catalogues use) and convert J2000 -> date before indigo_radec_to_altaz() if so, or convert at the call sites; reproduce first with a reference test (embedded JPL Horizons/independent values, synthetic site, fixed time via the existing scripting test time override), then fix; bump DRIVER_VERSION of each fixed driver; update the scripting/sequencer documentation that describes these functions (no README.md edits without approval - if a README needs a change, report it).

outcome.summary: Pass, no defects. indigo_agent_scripting.c:924-925 precesses J2000 ra (hours) / dec (deg) with indigo_j2k_to_eq(indigo_eq_of_date(UT2JD(now))) before indigo_radec_to_altaz(...,&now,...); same 'now' feeds equinox and LST, units match indigo_align.c:72-79 (ra*15*DEG2RAD), mirrors solar_altitude(). Callers: only Sequencer.js:1553/1561/1588 forward user ra/dec unchanged; scheduler bodies pass @target (J2000) as slew() does (Sequencer.js:1852 AGENT_MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES); no of-date caller; pointing paths untouched. Independent recomputation (own Python: IAU 2006 P03 precession, ERA-based GMST, main nutation terms, approx annual aberration) at 1704112496: case 1 apparent 6.9367 (ref 6.944816, -0.008), precession-only 6.9412 (-0.004), J2000-as-of-date 6.6199 (-0.325); case 2 apparent 23.6435 (+0.001), precession-only 23.6412 (-0.001), old 23.7894 (+0.147). Reference confirmed; 0.02 deg tolerance covers nutation/aberration omission yet is >7x below the smallest bug delta, so the test discriminates. Docs (Sequencer.md:148/150, mcp/agents/sequencer.md:86/88, scripting.md:105) accurate; no README changes. DRIVER_VERSION 0x03000014 > master 0x03000013; master changed only indigocat since merge base 2a0caefcb, git merge-tree against master is clean. Recorded whitespace and command-1 checks are on current tree 3edec2da; log shows 'PASS J2000 target altitude matches reference'. Limits: did not rerun tests; aberration in my check is approximate; flaky on-unload case not assessed.

history.text: Adding target altitude reference test to test_agent_scripting.c
Reproducing on old code: make test-agent-scripting
Check command-1 started: make Makefile.inc && make init && make -j8 -C indigo_libs all && make -C indigo_test test-agent-scripting test-agent-scripting-sequencer

Callers and frames: indigo_target_altitude() is called only from Sequencer.js steps wait_until_target_altitude_above() (lines 1553, 1561) and break_if_target_altitude_below() (line 1588), which forward the user's ra/dec unchanged. Scheduler task bodies pass scheduler_task.ra/dec from @target, documented as J2000 (INDIGO_SCHEDULER_GUIDE.md), the same frame slew()/precise_goto() send to AGENT_MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES. No caller in the repository passes coordinates of date, so converting inside the C binding cannot double-convert. Pointing paths are unchanged.

Reproduction: new case 'J2000 target altitude matches reference' in indigo_test/integration/test_agent_scripting.c, fixed time 2024-01-01 12:34:56 UTC (scripting_test_time override). References computed independently of INDIGO (IAU 1976 precession, IAU 1980 nutation main terms, annual aberration, GMST + equation of equinoxes; the same sidereal/horizon pipeline reproduces the JPL Horizons Sun elevations of the solar test within 0.004 deg): RA 10h Dec +20 at lat -30 lon -70 -> 6.944816 deg; RA 3h Dec +40 at lat 48.15 lon 17.11 -> 23.642420 deg; tolerance 0.02 deg. Old code: make -C indigo_test test-agent-scripting failed the case with 'target altitude 6.619793088395294 instead of 6.944816' (-0.325 deg, the precession since J2000).

Fix: target_altitude() in indigo_agent_scripting.c now precesses the J2000 ra/dec with indigo_j2k_to_eq(indigo_eq_of_date(UT2JD(now)), &ra, &dec) before indigo_radec_to_altaz(), as solar_altitude() does. DRIVER_VERSION 0x03000013 -> 0x03000014. Sequencer.js unchanged, so agent_scheduler's embedded Sequencer.js.dat needs no regeneration and the scheduler suite was not required. Docs: Sequencer.md, indigo_docs/mcp/agents/sequencer.md and scripting.md state J2000 input and precession-only conversion. After fix: flow check --command (build + test-agent-scripting test-agent-scripting-sequencer) passed, Scripting Agent 39/39, Sequencer.js 68/68; whitespace check passed. The pre-fix run also showed one unrelated 'on-unload execution' failure (has_message unload-ran) that did not recur on the post-fix run.

Test mapping: J2000 frame contract of indigo_target_altitude() -> test_agent_scripting 'J2000 target altitude matches reference' (two sites/hemispheres, error -0.32 and +0.15 deg if J2000 were used as of-date). Sequencer steps forwarding unchanged ra/dec -> existing test_agent_scripting_sequencer 'simulator altitude and hour angle' and sequencer_simulators.js sky cases (behavioural, limits +-91).
